title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Mr. Shh! (billed "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh)

won.source: Wrestling masked, pins Nighthawk at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998) with Legion of Pain interference; unmasks himself the next night on "Monday Mania" as Mr. Shh!

how: Won by pinfall, with outside interference.

lost.source: Retains through at least "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998, by double disqualification); no further document in the held record shows how or when the title left his hands.

note: A gap follows in the held record: by "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998) Chris Hart is described as a former World Champion who had already won and lost the title at least once by that point, and Night Stalker is shown holding it, won 'with the Jamaican Stud's help' from Hart. Neither the end of this reign nor Chris Hart's own first win is attested by any document this collection holds.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: "The Working Man" Chris Hart (second reign)

won.source: Pins The Night Stalker in 8:36 at "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998).

note: Still champion as of "November 20/21 Friday Fights"; a rematch against Night Stalker is booked for 12 December 1998, outside the held record.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Nighthawk

won.source: Billed champion, retaining in a falls-count-anywhere defense against Leon Redfield on the promotion's own 10 May 1998 home video, recapped within "Parade of Champions"; the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

lost.source: Loses to a masked "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh (revealed as Mr. Shh!) at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998) after Legion of Pain interference.

note: Recorded as champion from billing; no document in the held record shows how or when he won the title.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: "The Working Man" Chris Hart (first reign)

won.source: Not attested by any document this collection holds; recorded only from Chris Hart's own later on-air claim at "Clash of the Titans II" that Night Stalker and the Jamaican Stud "beat me for it together."

lost.source: Loses the title to The Night Stalker with the Jamaican Stud's assistance, per Chris Hart's own account; no document in the held record shows the match itself.

note: Presumed from Chris Hart's own on-air claim and his billing as a 'former HIWF World Champion' before Clash of the Titans II; grade presumed, not primary-source, since the win and loss are not independently attested.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: The Night Stalker

won.source: Not attested by any document this collection holds; recorded from Chris Hart's own account (see r003) and this wing's own "Clash of the Titans II" press release, which shows him as reigning champion entering that show.

lost.source: Loses to Chris Hart at "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998).

note: Also survives a separate 'controversial' title defense against Chris Hart the Saturday before Clash of the Titans II, per that show's own press release; that match's own result is not stated and is not treated as a further reign change here. Also stripped of the Television Championship the same week under a one-title-per-wrestler rule -- see the Television Championship's own reign r004.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-us-heavyweight-championship
label: Mantua Thunder

won.source: Pins Hellfire with a chair-assisted flying bulldog at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998).

how: Won by pinfall, using a chair.

lost.source: Retains against James Kira later the same night, and against Vic Valiant on "Monday Mania" (11 August 1998); no further document in the held record shows how or when the title left his hands.

note: By "November 20 Friday Fights" the Jamaican Stud is shown holding the title instead; the transition is not attested by any document this collection holds.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-us-heavyweight-championship
label: Hellfire

won.source: Billed champion, retaining a two-out-of-three-falls defense against "Foolkiller" Jason Bell at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

lost.source: Loses to Mantua Thunder at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998) after a chair shot.

note: Recorded as champion from billing; no document in the held record shows how or when he won the title.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-us-heavyweight-championship
label: "Jamaican Juggalo" the Jamaican Stud

won.source: Not attested by any document this collection holds; first shown as reigning champion on "November 20 Friday Fights."

note: Retains against Mantua Thunder by disqualification (foreign-object powder) on "November 20 Friday Fights"; the title itself does not change hands on a disqualification finish under the promotion's own rules.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
label: The Night Stalker

won.source: Pins Vic Valiant in 10:54 at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998), his first Television Championship.

lost.source: Loses to Tony Sanders by pinfall on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" after Legion of Pain interference (Jay Hawke's chair shot, followed by "Foolkiller" Jason Bell knocking out Tony Sanders and placing him atop Stalker for the pin).

note: Retains against Vic Valiant ("June 26 Friday Fights"), Bomb ("July 4 Friday Fights"), Aero ("July 10 Friday Fights"), and Jay Hawke ("Super Bowl of Wrestling II," 21 July 1998) before losing it.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
label: Tony Sanders

won.source: Wins the title on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" after Legion of Pain interference leaves The Night Stalker pinned "under questionable means."

how: Won by pinfall, with outside interference.

lost.source: By "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998), the Television Championship is shown vacant and The Night Stalker -- not Sanders -- is the one stripped of it under a one-title-per-wrestler rule; no document in the held record shows how or when Sanders lost the title to Stalker.

note: A further untracked transition: Night Stalker holds the Television Championship again by November, alongside the World Heavyweight Championship, triggering the promotion's own rule against holding two titles at once.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
label: "Stone Cold" Steve Anderson (billed masked as Tyrone the Psychopathic Soldier)

won.source: Wins the sixteen-man tournament final over Tony Sanders in 3:38 at "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998), unmasking afterward.

how: Won a single-elimination tournament final by pinfall (Stone Cold Stunner).
note: Retains against Tony Sanders by count-out on "November 20 Friday Fights" after voluntarily leaving the ring mid-match; the title does not change hands on a count-out under the promotion's own rules.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
label: "Double V" Vic Valiant

won.source: Billed champion entering "Parade of Champions," with commentary noting he has held "every title currently available except the World Title" and "two TV Title reigns"; the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

lost.source: Loses to The Night Stalker, who wins his first Television Championship, at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998), the culmination of Stalker's own HIWF Gauntlet run.

note: Recorded as champion from billing; no document in the held record shows how or when he won this particular reign.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
label: The Night Stalker (second reign)

won.source: Not attested by any document this collection holds; recorded only from the promotion's own "Clash of the Titans II" press release, which states he is being stripped of the title.

lost.source: Stripped by President J. Adam Hawkins ahead of "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998) under a rule barring one wrestler from holding two HIWF titles at the same time -- he had also won the World Heavyweight Championship by this point.

note: The sixteen-man tournament originally announced as a World Heavyweight Championship number-one-contender tournament is repurposed on the spot to crown the new, vacant Television Champion.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-cruiserweight-championship
label: El Diablo Rolande

won.source: Pins The Usurper in 14:18 with the Backflip Legdrop on "Friday Fights" (15 May 1998), recapped within "June 12 Friday Fights"; the originating document itself is outside the held record's corpus.

lost.source: Loses back to The Usurper on "Friday Fights" (29 May 1998), also recapped within "June 12 Friday Fights."

note: Both the win and the loss are recapped, not originally served, documents; cited here as primary-source recap footage rather than the originating broadcasts, which lie outside the held record's corpus.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-cruiserweight-championship
label: The Usurper (fourth reign, by his own count)

won.source: Pins El Diablo Rolande with a bridging back suplex in 5:22 on "Friday Fights" (29 May 1998), recapped within "June 12 Friday Fights"; commentary calls it "his fourth Cruiserweight Title."

lost.source: Loses to Alucard Belmont on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998).

note: Retains against El Diablo Rolande in a rematch on "June 12 Friday Fights" before losing it three days later.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-cruiserweight-championship
label: Alucard Belmont

won.source: Beats The Usurper for the title on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998).

note: Retains against El Diablo Rolande at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998, 14:09), against The Usurper at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998, 11:41), and against Vic Valiant by disqualification on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" (14:18) after Aero's ringside interference.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-tag-team-championship
label: The Predators

won.source: Billed champions, retaining the title over Hellfire and Serial Killa of the Apocalypse on "Monday Mania" (22 June 1998); no document in this record shows how or when they won it.

lost.source: No document in this record shows how or when the title left The Predators' hands.

note: Recorded as champions from billing; a large, untracked gap separates this reign from the Insano Boys' own 2001 reign.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-tag-team-championship
label: Insano Boys

won.source: Already billed World Tag Team Champions by the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast; no document in this record shows how or when they won the title.

how: Retains over Johnny Pyro and The Stud by disqualification on "Superstar Challenge" (7 September 2001).
note: Still champions as of 7 September 2001, with a defense against the Legion of Pain (Nighthawk and Viper) announced for "Clash of the Titans VII" (9 October 2001, outside this record).

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Mr. Shh! (second reign)

won.source: Already champion, and by then also described as the owner of the Supreme Wrestling Federation, when he retains over new Silent Assassins recruit Randall Flagg at "Clash of the Titans VI: Class Dismissed" (9 May 2000); no document in this record shows how or when he regained the title after his first reign.

lost.source: The promotion's own retrospective broadcast (9 September 2001) states he "would hold onto that title for another two months before finally losing it to Pagan"; the title change itself is not otherwise attested in this record.

note: A gap follows the earlier-held reign of Chris Hart (world-r005) and this reign; neither the end of Hart's reign nor the start of this one is attested by any document this record holds.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: Pagan

won.source: The promotion's own retrospective broadcast (9 September 2001) states Mr. Shh! "would hold onto that title for another two months before finally losing it to Pagan," roughly two months after 9 May 2000; the title change itself is not otherwise attested in this record.

lost.source: No document in this record shows how or when the title left Pagan's hands.

note: By the time of the reopened 2001 HIWF's own World Heavyweight Title tournament, The Stud is billed champion; no document in this record attests to the tournament's own final or to how The Stud won the title.

title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: The Stud

won.source: First found billed World Champion in the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast; the reopened HIWF's own World Heavyweight Title tournament (which The Stud entered as a bye-round competitor on 27 April and 25 May 2001) is presumed to have crowned him, but no document in this record shows its own semifinal, final, or how he won the title.

note: Still champion as of 9 September 2001, announced to defend the title against El Cholo at "Clash of the Titans VII" (9 October 2001, outside this record).
